page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c24g1.24xlarge is a GPU-accelerated compute instance powered by Intel Xeon 8163 processors running at 2.5 GHz. The configuration delivers 96 vCPUs (48 physical cores across 2 threads per core) built on x86_64 architecture, supported by 33 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates 372 GB of system RAM, providing approximately 3.88 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is provided by four NVIDIA Turing T4 GPUs delivering a combined 64 GB of VRAM. It operates on the KVM hypervisor with 30 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, while including no local storage.

Benchmark evaluations indicate a pronounced contrast between single-threaded and parallel processing. The single-core stress-ng score of 1103.89 and single-threaded gzip compression at 19.2 GB/sec rank in the lower percentiles, consistent with the modest 2.5 GHz base clock rate. However, total multi-core execution scales effectively, with a stress-ng multi-core benchmark of 70574.45 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieving 287.37 GB/sec, placing both in the top 25%. Cached memory read throughput reaches 3924.63 GB/sec, while large-block uncached read and write benchmarks register at 147.24 GB/sec and 58.43 GB/sec, respectively.

Network and throughput tests show 34.07 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks alongside strong in-memory key-value processing, reaching 64.27 million operations per second on Redis SET tests. Because the instance lacks bundled local storage, storage-heavy workflows require external network-attached volumes, making network utilization and architecture design critical factors. Qualitative cost efficiency favors parallel computing and inference pipelines that fully engage the four Turing GPUs and high core density rather than jobs bound by single-core speed.

This server type is appropriate for distributed machine learning inference, video transcoding pipelines, computer vision workloads, and parallel scientific computing. Its substantial memory footprint and high parallel throughput also support large-scale in-memory caching and distributed batch processing architectures.
